subject: System Design
title: Read-Heavy vs Write-Heavy Systems
description: Learn Read-Heavy vs Write-Heavy Systems in one minute.

hook.text: Twitter has 500 million tweet reads per second but only 6,000 new tweets per second. That's read-heavy.

buildup.text: Read-heavy systems optimize for fast retrieval: caching, replicas, and denormalized data.

discovery.text: Write-heavy systems like logging platforms optimize for fast ingestion: append-only logs and batch writes.

twist.text: The same data can be in both: write-optimized for ingestion, then transformed into a read-optimized view.

climax.text: Understanding your read/write ratio is the first step in designing the right data architecture.

punchline.text: Know your ratio — it shapes every decision.

quiz.question: What characterizes a read-heavy system?
options: Far more data reads than writes
